name: Client Status
desc: Client sends a status update: respawn after death or open inventory (to achieve).
notes: PERFORM_RESPAWN is sent when the player clicks "Respawn" after death. REQUEST_STATS opens the statistics screen.

writeup.p: C16 carries one enum state: PERFORM_RESPAWN, REQUEST_STATS, or OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT. It is the client's status signal for lifecycle events: respawn after death, stats/achievement screen state, and the open-inventory achievement that vanilla fires when the player presses E. The server's processClientStatus switches on the enum: PERFORM_RESPAWN recreates the player entity (with hardcore and end-conquest special cases), REQUEST_STATS flushes the stat file, OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT triggers the openInventory achievement.

processClientStatus: for PERFORM_RESPAWN it checks the end-conquest flag, hardcore bans, and that the player's health is <= 0 before recreating the player entity. REQUEST_STATS calls getStatFile().func_150876_a. OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT triggers AchievementList.openInventory. Notably the OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT state has no state validation: the client can claim its inventory opened at any time, which is exactly what inventory managers and disablers abuse to fake the inventory-open state.

AutoArmor (Sigma, Spicy) sends OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT in FakeInv mode so the server believes the inventory is open, letting shift-clicks register outside a real GUI. Inventory managers (Spicy InventoryManager, Rise Manager) track and force the open state with C16. InvMove/CancelInventoryMove (Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x) cancel the C16 open so the server never learns the player is in a GUI while moving. Disablers (Rise 5.99 Disabler sends PERFORM_RESPAWN; Rise 6.2.4 WatchdogDisabler sends OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT before click-window abuse) use the status packet to reset server-side player state. Spicy ChestStealer and Bhop reference C16 for the open-inventory close trick.

PERFORM_RESPAWN resets the player entity: position, health, and the hasMoved flag. Sending it outside death (Rise 5.99 Disabler c16 mode) recreates the player and can clear server-side tracking state, which is a classic anti-cheat reset vector. OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT with no real GUI open desyncs the server's inventory-open flag; clients then move and click while the server thinks the container is open, which InventoryMove modules pair with C0E clicks. The achievement trigger also fires a stat, so spam shows up in stat logs.

implementation.overview: The lifecycle status packet. AutoArmor fakes an open inventory with it, InventoryManagers force the open state, InvMove cancels it to hide GUI usage, and disablers fire PERFORM_RESPAWN to reset the server's view of the player. The open-inventory enum has zero state validation, which is the whole game.
implementation.server_handling: processClientStatus switches on the enum. PERFORM_RESPAWN: end-conquest recreate, hardcore ban/kick paths, then recreatePlayerEntity only when health <= 0. REQUEST_STATS: flush stat file. OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT: trigger the achievement; no check that a GUI is actually open. markPlayerActive is called on every status packet.
implementation.protocol_notes: Fields: VarInt enum ordinal (0 = PERFORM_RESPAWN, 1 = REQUEST_STATS, 2 = OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT). Sent in PLAY state. Vanilla fires OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT from GuiInventory open; modules send it from tick handlers. The enum is the only payload, so spoofing is a one-int forge.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Anti-cheats correlate OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT with the actual GUI state: opening the inventory while moving is the InventoryMove flag, so CancelInventoryMove cancels the C16 rather than the movement. PERFORM_RESPAWN outside death is a strong reset-abuse signal on servers that track entity recreation; Rise 5.99 gates it behind a packet-cooldown so it does not spam. WatchdogDisabler pairs the C16 open with C0E clicks, and the PingSpoofComponent parks C16 in its blink class list so delayed status packets do not leak.

modules.name: AutoArmor (FakeInv)
modules.purpose: Equip the best armor automatically; in FakeInv mode, send C16 OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT so the server accepts shift-clicks without a real GUI.
modules.how_it_works: Sigma AutoArmor scans armor slots (4-8) and inventory slots (9-44), computes protection values, and shift-clicks the best piece via playerController.windowClick. When the mode is FakeInv, it first sends C16(OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT) so the server-side inventory-open flag is set, allowing the clicks to register as if the player pressed E.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventTick with a Timer; C16 via sendQueue.addToSendQueue.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: FakeInv is invisible to vanilla (the achievement trigger is harmless) but servers that mirror GUI state can notice clicks with no GUI. OpenInv mode avoids the C16 entirely by waiting for a real GUI.
modules.variations: Spicy AutoArmor.java mirrors the same pattern (C16 import + send in the equip loop). LiquidSense Dev's AutoArmor sends C16 OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT from its SimulateInventory path when no GuiInventory is open, runs the shift-click, then closes with C0D.

modules.name: InventoryManager / Manager
modules.purpose: Manage inventory state by tracking and forcing the C16 open-inventory flag.
modules.how_it_works: Spicy InventoryManager hooks the packet event: C0D close sets isInventoryOpen = false, C16 open sets it true, and openInv() sends C16(OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT) if not already open. Rise 5.99 Manager tracks the same flag and sends C16 open before item management, then C0D close when done.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventPacket (C16/C0D tracking); openInv/closeInv helpers send the packets.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The state tracking keeps the client's view of the container consistent, which avoids the container desyncs that flag InventoryMove checks. Forcing open without a GUI is only detectable server-side via GUI-state mirroring.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 Manager.java (openInventoryIfNecessary, line ~428) and Rise 6.2.4/6.1.30 Manager.java implement the same open/close tracking with C16.

modules.name: InvMove / CancelInventoryMove
modules.purpose: Cancel the C16 open-inventory status so the server never learns the player is in a GUI while moving and clicking.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 6.2.4 CancelInventoryMove cancels C16(OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT), C0B(OPEN_INVENTORY) and C0DPacketCloseWindow on the send event, while forcing movement keys in PreUpdate. Rise 5.99 InvMove goes further: it cancels the C16 open status and re-wraps C0E clicks with a C16 open + C0D close pair sent without events.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The server believes the inventory never opened, so inventory-move checks that gate on the open flag never trigger. The trade-off is that legit clicks sent while 'not open' can desync the container.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 InvMove.java performs the C16/C0E/C0D re-wrap; Rise 6.1.30 CancelInventoryMove.java matches 6.2.4.

modules.name: Disabler (status abuse)
modules.purpose: Fire C16 status packets (PERFORM_RESPAWN or OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT) to reset or fake server-side player state.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 5.99 Disabler's c16 mode sends C16(PERFORM_RESPAWN) on a cooldown to reset the server-side player entity, clearing anti-cheat tracking; it is paired with C13 abilities and C18 spectate sends in the same mode block. Rise 6.2.4 WatchdogDisabler sends C16(OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT) via sendUnregisteredPacket before replaying a cancelled C0E click, faking the open-inventory state during watchdog click abuse.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: PERFORM_RESPAWN outside death is a hard reset-abuse signal on servers that count entity recreations; the health > 0 guard in vanilla means the respawn is silently ignored unless the player is actually dead, which is why Rise 5.99's mode is paired with fall damage tricks. The C16-open + C0E trick only works while watchdog's click window is active.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 Disabler.java (c16 mode sends PERFORM_RESPAWN, line ~293); Rise 6.1.30 WatchdogDisabler.java matches 6.2.4.

modules.name: ChestStealer
modules.purpose: Automatically empty chests; references C16 open-inventory to force the GUI state while stealing.
modules.how_it_works: Spicy ChestStealer spawns a thread on EventOpenChest that iterates the chest slots and shift-clicks each one with a randomized delay (250ms + 40ms jitter). The C16(OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT) send is present but commented out in this build; the active path uses spicyHandleMouseInput on the chest container.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventOpenChest (pre phase) starts the steal thread.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The randomized delay mimics human click timing; the thread-per-chest design is the detectable part (click cadence is uniform). The commented C16 shows the intended open-inventory close trick was disabled in this build.
modules.variations: Unique to Spicy in this corpus; other clients' chest stealers route through C0E clicks or C16 open state in their inventory managers.

modules.name: LuaEventPacket
modules.purpose: Expose C16 to November's Lua scripting API as id 0x16 with direction, for scripted inventory-status handling.
modules.how_it_works: packetIds maps C16PacketClientStatus.class to 0x16; the wrapper stores the id and 'out' direction from the EventPacket for Lua-side matching.

implementation.general_hooks: PacketSendEvent (cancel C16 open), tick handlers (send C16 open), packet receive tracking (C16/C0D state machines). Spicy hooks EventPacket; Rise 6.x uses EventLink listeners and sendUnregisteredPacket. LiquidSense Dev sends C16 from a render tick in AutoArmor; November Recode 2.0 cancels C16 on EventPacket.Out in InventoryWalkModule and exposes 0x16 to scripts.
implementation.client_variations: Rise 5.99 sends C16 via sendQueue.addToSendQueue or PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent. Rise 6.2.4 uses sendUnregisteredPacket to bypass its own event system (and the PingSpoofComponent parks C16 in its blink tuple). Sigma/Spicy push raw packets to the send queue. Tenacity references C16 only in PacketUtil in this corpus. LiquidSense Dev's C16 open is paired with an immediate C0D close after the click batch; November Recode 2.0's InventoryWalkModule uses a two-mode Setting (VANILLA/CANCEL) and cancels via event.setCanceled(true).

anticheat.overview: The client status packet is a lifecycle signal: PERFORM_RESPAWN after death and OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT to open the statistics screen. Server-side anticheats use it in two ways. Respawn handling resets movement, inventory and combat state so the player starts clean after death, and a respawn command sent at the wrong time is a disabler signature. The open-inventory command also toggles the state that inventory-move and inv-tweak checks rely on, because moving while a screen is open is what inventory move cheats do.

checks.name: InventoryB (Frequency)
checks.purpose: Detects the open-inventory-achievement spam that inventory move and inventory tweak modules use to move while a screen is open.
checks.how_it_works: PacketCheck on WrappedPlayInClientCommand. When the command is OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT it sets the inventory flag; while the flag is set, if the player is attacking or swinging with less than 60 ms since the last flying packet, a buffer increments and fails at 3. Any flying packet clears the flag and refreshes lastFlying. The threshold of 3 keeps it tolerant of legitimate statistics-screen opens.
checks.detects: Inventory move, inventory tweak, and modules that keep the inventory state open while attacking.
checks.variations: CheaterDeleter InventoryMoveCheck keys the same state off the vanilla client-command listener; AutoEye InventoryWalk flags position changes while the inventory event is open.

checks.name: DisablerRespawn (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Flags PERFORM_RESPAWN commands sent while the player is not dead, the classic disabler that resets server-side state without dying.
checks.how_it_works: PacketHandler that reads GPacketPlayClientClientCommand. If the command is PERFORM_RESPAWN and the Bukkit player is not actually dead, a buffer increments and logs a violation at 3. Flying packets decay the buffer by 0.0125 per packet so lag does not accumulate it. The check annotation sets threshold 3.
checks.detects: Respawn disablers, respawn spam, and clients that send the respawn command to reset check state without a death.
checks.variations: NoCheatPlus validates respawn timing inside its moving checks; Frequency treats the packet only as inventory state; Grim resets its check state on the respawn flow instead of flagging.

checks.name: InventoryMoveCheck (CheaterDeleter)
checks.purpose: Flags movement while a container screen is open, using the vanilla client-command listener to track open state.
checks.how_it_works: Registers a ClientCommandC2SPacketListener plus movement, packet and damage listeners. While the player has a current screen handler open and changes position, it records the open time and inspects each move: upward movement with falling velocity, or horizontal acceleration in an axis where the server velocity is zero, flags Inventory Move. The first 500 ms after opening are ignored, damage resets the deltas, and closing the screen clears the open flag.
checks.detects: Inventory move, inventory walk and inv-tweak movement while a screen is open.
checks.variations: AutoEye InventoryWalk flags the same behavior with a one-line condition and reverts by closing the inventory; Frequency InventoryB catches the open-command spam itself; Photon InventoryMove runs on the open state from its own tracker.

checks.name: Respawn state reset (Grim)
checks.purpose: Rebuilds the simulation state when the respawn flow runs, so checks do not carry stale data across a death.
checks.how_it_works: PacketPlayerRespawn listens to the server-side respawn, join-game and health packets that follow the client's PERFORM_RESPAWN command. On UPDATE_HEALTH with health below zero it marks the self entity dead, and on RESPAWN it forces the player to accept a teleport before movements are processed, clears positions, resets ground, sneak, sprint and known-input state, resets several badpackets checks, and clears chunk and entity caches on a dimension change. The client half of the flow is the C16 PERFORM_RESPAWN command.
checks.detects: Not a flagging check; it prevents respawn-related desync and disablers that rely on stale check state.
checks.variations: Artemis DisablerRespawn flags premature respawn commands; NCP resets its move queue on respawn events inside the moving checks.

checks.name: InventoryWalk (AutoEye)
checks.purpose: Flags position changes while the inventory event is active and the client should be frozen.
checks.how_it_works: Check of type INVENTORY_EVENT: it fires when the client reports the open-inventory event. The check passes only if the player moved, lastFlying is zero, physics say the player is moving, the server velocity is zero on both horizontal axes, and less than 60 ms passed since the last move. On a pass it reverts by closing the player's inventory.
checks.detects: Inventory walk where the player moves while the inventory screen is open.
checks.variations: CheaterDeleter InventoryMoveCheck and Photon InventoryMove detect the same cheat with more tolerant timing; Frequency InventoryB catches the open-command spam that precedes it.
